quest.title: Cleansing Light
quest.description: The Adventurers' Guild in Inazuma seems to have a commission concerning the Sacred Sakura...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x525, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: #Ad astra abyssosque, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Recently, the Adventurers' Guild has received an unusual commission, and after careful consideration, we believe that—

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "The traveler would be the most suitable candidate." Right?

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: Hehe, indeed. As ever.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: I will spare the pleasantries, then. May I ask if you two are available to help?

choices.text: Of course, that's what we're here for.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Well, let me go over it briefly. Our client for this job is the Yashiro Commission. Apparently, rifthounds are attacking the roots of the Sacred Sakura nearby Mt. Yougou in great numbers.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Rifthounds? ...On Narukami Island?

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Yes. We are not sure where exactly these creatures come from. But this time, they are attacking in alarming numbers with great aggression and a clear target.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: The Sacred Sakura is of tremendous importance to Inazuma. I trust you are aware of this already?

choices.text: I believe I understand.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Good. Then you can see that this case is very urgent indeed.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is the Tenryou Commission aware?

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Yes, and they are already taking action of their own. However, given that the Sacred Sakura's root system is vast and complex, and faced with the unpredictability and scale of the rifthounds' attacks, they are finding it difficult to defend against them.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Their main priority is to protect the civilian population. So they are actively looking to cooperate with all other available forces to eliminate the monsters.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: The Adventurers' Guild is one of the key parties assisting the Tenryou Commission with their work. But so far, the combined efforts to combat the rifthounds has failed to substantially ameliorate the situation.

choices.text: Time to make some whelps yelp.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: You have our deepest gratitude. Your confident response puts me far more at ease.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: I will mark on your map the areas where rifthound appearances have been recently reported. I hope you won't encounter too much trouble overcoming them.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Relax! We'll be back before you can say "ad astra abyssosque."

choices.text: I'll send these pooches packing.
I'm hazy.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: For a long time, the Sacred Sakura has been absorbing filth from Inazuma's Ley Lines to maintain stability in the land.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: If it were ever damaged, the filth would once again invade Inazuma, causing great catastrophe. That's why this is a rather urgent case.

choices.text: It'll depend on the task and the compensation.

talks.objective: Go to the area where the monsters have appeared

dialogues.speaker: Raiden Shogun?
dialogues.text: Torn to oblivion!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sh—Shogun? Wait, no... could also be Ei...

dialogues.speaker: Raiden Shogun?
dialogues.text: ...It's you two.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: It has been a long time. We have not seen each other since the resolution of the Tenryou Commission crisis.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, sounds more like Ei... it is you, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You sure made short work of them. That was amazing!

choices.text: ...What are you doing here?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: I'm making early preparations for what is to come.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Last time we took a walk around Inazuma together, I witnessed the way the world is today. I was finally able to comprehend some things that I had never understood in the past.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Since then, every time I encounter an obstacle in my thinking, I find myself having the urge to spend some time in the outside world.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Makes sense. You must get super bored being stuck in there all the time.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: ...Might I remind you that I am not here to amuse myself.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Recently, I have observed a number of changes in the external world from the Plane of Euthymia. The most serious of these being the attack on the Sacred Sakura by numerous rifthounds.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: I considered this matter worthy of my attention. So I pursued them, and they led me here, where I happened to run into you.

choices.text: But the Commissions and adventurers can deal with monsters.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: If the Shogun rather than I were to discover them... Yes, perhaps she would have left the situation alone.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm? Why? Because she's just a puppet?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Precisely. According to the rules I designed for her, matters of this nature are to be delegated to the Tri-Commission.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: But rifthounds attacking the Sacred Sakura... it brings back bad memories of that terrible disaster...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A disaster?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Yes. Five hundred years ago, a great catastrophe befell Inazuma.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Everything was engulfed in a pitch-black fog and monsters ravaged the land... Countless lives were lost, and this homeland that the people had worked so hard to build barely escaped being obliterated entirely.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: The monsters committed many atrocities on Inazuman soil. And the rifthounds were always their advance guard.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Their duty was to tear open a passage through space with their claws and teeth, and then call in even more powerful beasts.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Five hundred years ago... Khaenri'ah.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Hmm. So you've heard of it, too.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: That's an episode of history that I am loath to recall. Maybe to you, it seems like my response to these creatures was an excessive one.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: But an excess of caution is not unwarranted in this case.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Guess you can't argue with that...

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Since we are both here for the same reason, let us work together.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: From the traces they've left in the surrounding area, there should be many more monsters nearby. All of them must be eliminated.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let's go.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon feels so safe when we're in Ei's company! Having someone uber-powerful on your team kinda makes you feel invincible, doesn't it?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, yeah — after we've dealt with the monsters, we should ask her to tell us more about Khaenri'ah.

choices.text: It doesn't seem like a matter needing the archon's attention...
What brings you out this time?

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: We are lucky... the damage is not too serious. The Yashiro Commission will be able to nurse the root system back to health.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This stuff that's flowing out, is it sap or something? And how come it's glowing...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh—What's this?

choices.text: Is someone injured?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Could they be... dead people? It wouldn't be the first time we'd seen ghosts on our journey.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But... why would they appear here?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Let's search the area. Perhaps we will find out.

response.speaker: Kitamura
response.text: Ugh... ugh...

response.speaker: Kitamura
response.text: I can't go on like this... not when the other troops are counting on me...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What happened here? Could you tell us?

response.speaker: Kitamura
response.text: Who are you? What are you doing here?

response.speaker: Kitamura
response.text: Run, quick, while you still can! The monsters will be back... And once you're in their sights, I'm telling you — there's no escaping them!

response.speaker: Kitamura
response.text: We will defend Inazuma... until our dying breath!

choices.text: What exactly happened?

response.speaker: Kitamura
response.text: You... you don't know? Inazuma is engulfed in darkness.

response.speaker: Kitamura
response.text: Beasts and horrifying monsters are everywhere! They are merciless, ferocious... and they will devour everything in their path...

response.speaker: Kitamura
response.text: Every last trace of humanity's existence, I tell you... they'll devour it all...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But look... none of that seems to be going on around here.

response.speaker: Kitamura
response.text: Not right now, but they'll be back... Look — get out of here, now!!! There's no time left!

response.speaker: Kitamura
response.text: The Almighty Shogun is gone, so is Kitsune Saiguu. There's no one left to rely on but ourselves.

response.speaker: Kitamura
response.text: I don't know how long we can hold out for, but... if we abandon our hope, then we've got nothing left at all.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Don't worry. I am right here.

response.speaker: Kitamura
response.text: It's... the Shogun!?

response.speaker: Kitamura
response.text: You're back!

response.speaker: Kitamura
response.text: Please, we beg you... you have to help us... you have to save Inazuma!

response.speaker: Kitamura
response.text: Only the glow of your supreme lightning can dispel this terrible darkness... please, or the whole of Inazuma will be reduced to a hunting ground for the beasts!

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Calm down. The war you speak of is over.

response.speaker: Kitamura
response.text: Over? But... what do you mean, Shogun...

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Look around you. The grass grows green and lush and a soft breeze blows. This is Inazuma at peace, as you will no doubt remember.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: There are no monsters, nor is there anything else here that could threaten your life.

response.speaker: Kitamura
response.text: Hmm...

response.speaker: Kitamura
response.text: But... how? Just moments ago, they were everywhere...

response.speaker: Kitamura
response.text: I saw them tear my comrade to shreds with my own eyes...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, calm down! Everything's fine now!

response.speaker: Kitamura
response.text: Huh...

response.speaker: Kitamura
response.text: I think I understand... Almighty Shogun... you saved Inazuma!

response.speaker: Kitamura
response.text: Yes... we were right to place our trust in the Almighty Shogun. As long as the Shogun is with us, Inazuma will last for an eternity...

response.speaker: Kitamura
response.text: Thank you, Your Excellency, thank you, thank you...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wh—What's wrong with him?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Is he disappearing?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: ...He's gone.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Paimon can't even begin to understand what that was all about... but somehow, Paimon feels all sad and hopeless...

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: If I am not mistaken, what we just saw was a samurai's memory that was buried in the land.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: The Sacred Sakura can absorb and purify the filth in the Ley Lines. After the rifthounds attacked, some of this filth leaked out through the cracks in the trunk and formed a physical entity.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: An entity formed with strong filth would be highly aggressive. But when purified, it presents in the form of a memory.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Purified filth quickly dissipates and will be absorbed by the Ley Lines shortly afterwards. In other words, it cannot exist for too long.

choices.text: I see...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So the memories of the ones that died are all appearing at this moment?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Yes. That soldier was one of the many thousands who made the ultimate sacrifice. What he was describing just now was precisely the disaster that happened in Inazuma 500 years ago.

choices.text: He mentioned that the Shogun was absent...

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Yes. Inazuma was facing many great crises at that time. Some were local in origin, while others... others came from the now-fallen kingdom of Khaenri'ah.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: The disaster in Inazuma caused me great concern. I felt that I had to step in before it was too late, otherwise it would spread to all of Teyvat.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: But my friend, Kitsune Saiguu, reassured me that I had nothing to worry about. She would shoulder the responsibility of protecting Inazuma, and mobilize all forces at her disposal to combat the threat.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: ...I could tell that although neither of us acknowledged it, we both knew that the road ahead would likely end in tragedy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So... Inazuma was attacked at the same time as when the disaster happened in Khaenri'ah?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Indeed. Countless monsters suddenly appeared throughout all of Inazuma. In the end... Kitsune Saiguu sacrificed her life to protect the people.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: I never had the chance to see her one last time. But I would like to believe that she kept her promise to me until the very last.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: But even then, Inazuma was left more devastated than we could have ever imagined. Those terrible tragedies left great wounds that are still felt to this day, both on the land itself... and in my heart.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ei...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Is this the "loss" that Yae Miko mentioned?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Yes. For the longest time, I couldn't bring myself to face the pain of that loss.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: All my martial might was in vain... Though I could conquer Tatarigami and vanquish monsters, I was helpless against the ravages of time, powerless to keep the ones I cherished alive.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: But after my clash with human ambition, I thought long and hard. Now I realize I cannot fixate on the past forever.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So you're no longer stuck in the past?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: ...When I traveled around Inazuma with you, I caught a glimpse of how the nation has progressed over the centuries. A glimpse of human potential. Everything far exceeded my expectations.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Moving forward inevitably invites further loss, but also new encounters.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Just think of that soldier. Despite all the losses he had experienced, he still chose to keep fighting, for the sake of moving forward.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: All those who sacrificed themselves back then gave their lives fighting for a future... but perhaps the future they were hoping for is not the eternity that I once strove for.

choices.text: Absolutely.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: As Inazuma's god, it is high time I honored their wishes.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Warriors of the past who spilled your blood on this land, your noble souls now rest in this earth.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: I will never forget you, and all that you did for Inazuma.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ei's taking all this pretty hard...

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Come on. Let's keep investigating the damage to the Sacred Sakura.

choices.text: That's what being human is about.
He mentioned that Kitsune Saiguu was absent...
The same thing happened to Dusky Ming.
What monsters?
How terrible.

talks.objective: Look for the marks left behind
Look for the marks left behind

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, where'd he go?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He wouldn't have gone looking for a tea set himself, would he?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wouldn't put it past him...

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Or perhaps the Ley Lines did not have the power to sustain him for very long. As was the case with the memory we saw earlier.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... so we won't get to drink his tea?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We didn't even have a chance to say goodbye... *sobs*

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: The information held in the Ley Lines is complex and disorderly. The fact that we were able to meet him to begin with was a miracle of fate...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mmm...

choices.text: Cheer up, Paimon.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Well, this chance won't come often, and we do have a tea set. Perhaps I should try my hand at making us a pot of tea.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: I've watched Furuyama brew tea on many occasions... I doubt I should have any major problems doing it myself.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Ei brews a piping-hot pot of tea with the tea set.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: The tea is ready, please give it a try.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: So many thoughts were racing through my head as I was brewing it, I... I'm not sure how to explain it...

choices.text: You don't need to. I understand.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: You're right, but the things we've seen today have brought back many memories for me.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: I've been reminded of many people, too. Kitsune Saiguu, Makoto, and all the other friends who I watched pass even further back.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Back at the Yashiro Commission, I kept the conversation reasonably light-hearted. But now... I'd like to broach a heavier topic, if I may.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: The events of 500 years ago not only robbed me of my friend, Kitsune Saiguu... they also took Makoto away from me for good.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She died in that disaster too?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Yes. She went to Khaenri'ah alone, without telling me.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Unlike me, Makoto was no martial artist. Whenever similar crises had arisen in the past, I was always the one to face them in her stead.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: But this time, the circumstances were so grave that Makoto had no choice but to leave me behind. Or... perhaps it was more that she went ahead of me, put herself in front of me so that I would remain hidden. In any case, by the time I realized what was happening...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Makoto had already...

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Yes. It was too late. I arrived only in time to hear her dying breath.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: She had already lapsed into unconsciousness by that point, so all I could do was enter into her mind... As far as you're concerned, it would be somewhere similar to the Plane of Euthymia.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: It was there that we bid each other a final farewell. I cried bitterly. Even in those final moments, I couldn't understand her actions.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Why did she go to Khaenri'ah first, and not I? Why did she keep me in the dark about it? Was it to shield me?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: It was there and then that I resolved to pursue eternity. As a testament to that decision, I saved her realm of consciousness just before it collapsed completely, and brought it back to Inazuma.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's quite a story...

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: When I returned to Inazuma, I was shocked to find that a great sakura tree had appeared on Mt. Yougou. The tree that you know as the Sacred Sakura.

choices.text: ..."Appeared"?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: That's exactly what everyone back then told me as well. That it had existed since time immemorial. They were so matter-of-fact about it, and couldn't at all understand what I was so surprised about.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: No one questioned it, and yet its presence contrasted so starkly with the area as I remembered it... it seemed as if I was the only one to have noticed it appear suddenly out of thin air.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: In the end, I simply had to accept that it was a miraculous effect of Makoto's consciousness.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: With the help of the Sacred Sakura's power, I was finally able to overcome the monsters and quell the disaster in Inazuma.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This is all really hard to understand... Kinda beyond Paimon's level.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Simply put, Makoto's power somehow made that tree appear.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Yes... She had such a great love for this land, and for its people. In this respect, I still do not compare to her.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: I once told myself that I would never speak of these events again. Facing the fact that she is gone is unbearably painful.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: But even the tea that is most bitter to the tongue, once swallowed, leaves some sweetness in the throat.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: ...And it's time I came to terms with it all.

choices.text: It seems like you've done a lot of thinking about this already.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, um, while we're on the topic, since you experienced that battle in person...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: #Have you seen my {F#brother}{M#sister} before?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: #{F#Brother}{M#Sister}? Hmm... I had heard that you were looking for your family.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: #You mean to say that {F#he}{M#she} was somehow involved in the Khaenri'ah disaster?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Based on what we've learned so far, it seems so, yeah.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: I'm sorry. I wasn't there for the whole thing. By the time I arrived, the worst of the fighting was already over.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: And also... my mind was consumed entirely with the plight of Inazuma and the fate of those closest to me.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: So I am afraid I can't help you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh... well that's a shame. But it can't be helped I guess...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Boy, both of you have experienced great tragedy...

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: With this last cup of tea, let us honor the tea master's memory.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Thank you, destiny, for giving us the chance to meet again.

choices.text: I know the pain of separation too.
The Sacred Sakura has always been there, hasn't it?
It's just the memories flooding back in...
Let's make our own tea.

talks.objective: Look for the marks left behind

dialogues.speaker: Furuyama
dialogues.text: After my eyes went bad, many aspects of daily life became much more challenging. But I always wanted to be a competent tea brewer, right to the end.

dialogues.speaker: Furuyama
dialogues.text: *sigh* But now, it looks like I have to rely on you.

talks.objective: Try to figure out what happened
Talk to the person who appeared

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, something seems wrong with Ei...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Are you feeling okay?

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Why would you ask that?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, usually, you'd pull out your sword and "swish," vaporize them all in one go, no?

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: You are unduly concerned. I'm simply conserving my energy.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Although I have some understanding of the situation already, it could take an unexpected turn at any time.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: I must be prepared for anything. If there are more formidable monsters lying in wait in this area, I must make sure I have the strength to face them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, makes sense! Spoken like a seasoned shogun.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The roots seem pretty badly damaged this time... We definitely need to tell the Yashiro Commission about this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, the same light is leaking out again.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is it the same situation as before?

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: ...Furuyama? Is that you?

dialogues.speaker: Furuyama
dialogues.text: Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Furuyama
dialogues.text: Almighty Shogun? What brings you back so soon? I thought you were off fighting a battle in a distant land?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Fighting a battle in a distant land? Sounds like this guy's talking about 500 years ago, too.)

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Allow me to introduce Furuyama. He is a tea master and a member of my retinue.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Though blind, Furuyama is unparalleled in his ability to appraise tea. He brews some of the very finest tea in all of Inazuma.

dialogues.speaker: Furuyama
dialogues.text: Your Excellency, you shower me with praise undeserved. I have simply had the good fortune to be in Your Excellency's presence long enough to become acquainted with all the skills that are required of me.

dialogues.speaker: Furuyama
dialogues.text: It sounds like the Almighty Shogun has brought a guest?

dialogues.speaker: Furuyama
dialogues.text: ...I'm afraid I am unable to serve you any respectable refreshments on account of the current situation... but please sit and rest.

dialogues.speaker: Furuyama
dialogues.text: After all... it's quite a mess out there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... what should we do?

choices.text: Let's go along with what he says.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, um... yeah, sheesh, there's monsters everywhere out there, it's pitch-black, and loads of people have been injured...

response.speaker: Furuyama
response.text: I see. So they have fought their way this far already.

response.speaker: Furuyama
response.text: Most of the residents in this neighborhood have already escaped. They wanted to take me with them, but it seemed rather pointless to me. So I decided to stay.

response.speaker: Furuyama
response.text: And now the Almighty Shogun is here, I have even less reason to run away, hehe.

response.speaker: Furuyama
response.text: Imagine, if this was something that even the Almighty Shogun was powerless to resolve, where could I possibly run to then?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: How come you're not panicking?

response.speaker: Furuyama
response.text: People flee out of a desire to live on. And the desire to live on stems from a feeling of having unfinished business in life.

response.speaker: Furuyama
response.text: But me? I have no such thoughts, and I have no regrets.

response.speaker: Furuyama
response.text: The Almighty Shogun often speaks to me about her dreams over tea.

response.speaker: Furuyama
response.text: Just listening to her stories, ahh... I've been blind for many years, but her vivid descriptions took me on a splendid journey to all the most beautiful places in Inazuma... Over time, I've come to understand her mindset. Quite the romantic at heart. A true dreamer.

response.speaker: Furuyama
response.text: One thing she always says is... "Good things don't last forever. Everything changes, fades, disappears completely over the passage of time. And so, people must make the most of the life they have, seize the chance to enjoy it while it lasts, and have no regrets in the end..."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Umm...

choices.text: (That doesn't sound like Ei at all...)

response.speaker: Furuyama
response.text: So you see, as bleak as things may be now, I have experienced countless wonderful things in life, and have no reason not to be satisfied.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Perhaps... you are right.

response.speaker: Furuyama
response.text: It won't be long now before I have to say goodbye to the Almighty Shogun for the last time. Ah, what a pity... I'll never get to see what Inazuma looks like after the Almighty Shogun rebuilds it anew.

response.speaker: Furuyama
response.text: But I suppose it doesn't matter. Everyone says that Inazuma has turned dark now... but to me, it went dark a long time ago.

response.speaker: Furuyama
response.text: Once this catastrophe is over, life is sure to spring forth anew. But even if I survived until then, I'd probably be a hopelessly befuddled old so-and-so by then... Hahaha, so never mind, eh.

response.speaker: Furuyama
response.text: Oh, goodness me. Speaking of befuddled, look at me rambling away to my heart's content and forgetting to serve the tea.

response.speaker: Furuyama
response.text: The Almighty Shogun comes to visit and I don't have the tea ready. A truly egregious loss of decorum.

response.speaker: Furuyama
response.text: One moment, I'll just... Hmm? Where in the world is the tea set?

response.speaker: Furuyama
response.text: I hope the others didn't smash it to smithereens in their hasty departure.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Can't see a tea set anywhere around here...

response.speaker: Furuyama
response.text: Really? But it's always been right by my side... Goodness gracious... What a fool I'm making of myself.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We know where to find a tea set.

response.speaker: Furuyama
response.text: I couldn't possibly have my guests fetch it themselves, that would be most discourteous indeed.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Don't worry about it. Take a rest, we'll be back right away.

response.speaker: Furuyama
response.text: Almighty Shogun, you're not going too, are you? No, no, no, your humble servant implores you... Not with the war raging outside...

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: This place is... complicated. It's quite unlike the tea house in your memories.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Leave it to us.

response.speaker: Furuyama
response.text: But... well, okay. I never thought I'd see the day that I need the Almighty Shogun to personally collect my tea set for me...

response.speaker: Furuyama
response.text: I can't decide whether it's a final regret or a final stroke of good fortune, haha.

choices.text: (This doesn't fit the definition of eternity at all.)
I want to learn more about the past.

talks.objective: Go to the Kamisato Estate to get a tea set

dialogues.speaker: Hirano
dialogues.text: It's the Traveler, and... the Almighty Shogun!

dialogues.speaker: Hirano
dialogues.text: How might I be of assistance, Your Excellency?

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: I wish to borrow a tea set from the Yashiro Commission.

dialogues.speaker: Hirano
dialogues.text: Oh, uh, sure! I'll fetch that for you right away.

dialogues.speaker: Hirano
dialogues.text: Uh, please step into the courtyard and have a rest, Almighty Shogun. Oh, and I'll inform my lord about your visit immediately. Ah, and the tea set, I'll bring that here as soon as it's ready...

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Be at ease, I'm not here to see Commissioner Kamisato. Actually, I'd prefer to spend this time chatting with the Traveler. Please, fetch the tea set at your convenience.

dialogues.speaker: Hirano
dialogues.text: No, no, no. I am your humble servant, I daren't think of my own convenience when the Almighty Shogun graces me with her presence! I'll deal with it right away.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Well, it's not often we have the chance to chat. I'm sure you must have a lot of questions?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Was it really you that that tea master used to serve?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right, Paimon wanted to ask that, too! The Almighty Shogun that he described didn't sound anything like you at all.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: I seldom had the time to drink tea. Any free time I had was spent practicing martial arts.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: So in the vast majority of cases, the one he made tea for was the former Electro Archon... who was also my sister. Raiden Makoto.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: He may well have had an inkling about there being two "Raiden Shoguns." But he always acted as if he was completely unaware of it.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: The philosophy of life that he shared with us just now, that was Makoto's view on reality. She always saw things that way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You and Makoto had pretty different views, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Indeed we did. It was the biggest difference between us.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: In her eyes, the most precious things in this world were dreams — the yearning for a better future held by living beings.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Dreams... or in other words, "ambitions"?

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: They are similar, but not identical.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: When you came charging into the Plane of Euthymia, I saw human aspirations light up the sky far above in the form of countless stars. This... somewhat shook me.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Now, it seems like she was right, while I took the wayward path.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow. There sure was a lot going on beneath the surface...

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Makoto saw a bigger picture than I did. In her view, a "dream" is more imaginary, more abstract than an "ambition."

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: An "ambition" is a yearning for something material, or a concrete outcome. It is finite in nature, and will be replaced by a new ambition in due course.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Makoto was more concerned with the force that drives humans to constantly generate new ambitions in the first place. It is something innate, rooted in instinct — in other words... it is something eternal.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's, uh, quite a lot to take in...

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: To put it simply, Makoto wasn't concerned about outcomes.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: I didn't understand at the time. How can we say that we are maintaining eternity when things are constantly moving forward and evolving?

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: I suppose what it comes down to is the definition of "eternity" she set out with.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It seems more in line with how humans view the world.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Yes, it does. I always thought that she must have grasped some elusive, arcane wisdom to arrive at the conclusions she did.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: But in the last analysis, Makoto's philosophy was — on the surface, at least — an elegantly simple one. Notwithstanding that it was also the more prudent choice, based on a more mature, far-sighted outlook.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you feel you're starting to understand her better now?

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: You have already witnessed my previous views on eternity.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: But now, I no longer cling to what was lost. I suppose that means our differences have been reconciled.

dialogues.speaker: Hirano
dialogues.text: Almighty Shogun, I found a tea set! This one in particular should be fit for Your Excellency's use...

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: It's quite beautiful. Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Hirano
dialogues.text: You are too kind, a humble servant such as I does not deserve the gratitude of the Almighty Shogun...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's all good, Sir! She's actually pretty chill.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Let us return. We ought not keep Furuyama waiting too long.

talks.objective: Go to where the tea master is

dialogues.speaker: Hirano
dialogues.text: Take care, Almighty Shogun. You too, Traveler... And you too, um, uh... y—you take care too, anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Sacred Sakura's in danger again, huh. Who'd have thought.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Keeping the Sacred Sakura safe was Hanachirusato's greatest wish, and now these mangy mutts are trying to destroy it. Time to teach them a lesson!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: They're attacking the Sacred Sakura! Stop them!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This color... It's similar to the color when the Sacred Sakura takes damage!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's follow it, it should be this way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: As expected, there are a load of rifthounds here, too.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Leave them to me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Where should we go to find a tea set?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Having a cup of tea isn't exactly the most urgent thing to do right now... but at the same time, this lovely old man from 500 years ago has been through so much, and it makes Paimon so sad...

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: I'm also feeling very nostalgic for his tea.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, why don't we go to the Kamisato Estate? There'll definitely be a tea set we can borrow there.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: I'm also feeling very nostalgic for his tea.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, why don't we go to the Kamisato Estate? There'll definitely be a tea set we can borrow there.
